## 固定收益市場主線

AI類股再度遭到拋售，加上美國醞釀新一輪關稅的消息，重新帶動避險需求，美國公債回升，但最長天期債券未能跟上。5年期殖利率下降2.87個基點至4.7331%，10年期下降1.4個基點至4.9297%，30年期則上升1.35個基點至5.3203%。消費者信心轉強、油價反彈，加上市場持續預期聯準會將升息，抑制了債市漲勢。

科技股風險偏好降溫，對個別公司債的衝擊更大。CoreWeave債券回吐週一漲幅，跌至歷史低點，美國整體高收益債利差則小幅擴大。輝達先前逆轉領導層人事決定，曾讓市場信心恢復一個交易日；週二交易再度將焦點拉回AI產業取得資金的能力與成本。

多個經濟體的貨幣政策訊號仍偏向緊縮。加拿大央行警告，累積的能源成本將愈來愈多地轉嫁給消費者，歐洲及英國官員也主張進一步升息。澳洲債券則因降息預期升溫而上漲，顯示全球通膨爭論之下，各地成長條件正出現差異。委內瑞拉新公布的主權債務資料，以及Visma擬議的數十億歐元融資，也為個別借款人帶來了重要進展。

## 美債回升遇上美國數據轉強

投資人再度質疑科技投資能否持續，美國市場部分逆轉週一撤出避險資產的走勢。那斯達克100指數下跌1.99%至26,214.17點，半導體指數重挫7.88%；輝達跌約6%，Anthropic則跌破$83的IPO價格。標普500指數僅下跌0.50%至7,201.09點，掩蓋了成分股表現的差異：多數個股上漲，道瓊指數也上漲0.9%。

華府準備對中國、歐盟及其他十多個經濟體商品加徵關稅的消息傳出後，賣壓加速。知情人士表示，這些措施將取代遭最高法院推翻的關稅。中國商品預計面臨較其他國家更廣的課徵範圍，但新增關稅仍會使整體稅率維持在各別貿易協議約定的水準內。美方正逐一針對各經濟體擬定措施，並非全面一體適用的關稅。

這項差異影響未來貿易衝擊的規模。美國貿易代表署預計將完成針對製造業產能過剩的301條款調查，作為擬議措施的依據。週二股市對消息作出反應時，美債也出現買盤；貿易不確定性再起，為AI需求疑慮再添壓力。

據Bloomberg盤中利率報導，10年期殖利率一度降至約4.90%，創兩週低點，隨後消費者信心轉強、原油價格回升，使債券回吐部分漲幅。最終收盤殖利率為4.9297%，收盤債價漲幅因而較盤中明顯收斂。高盛資產管理的Lindsay Rosner表示，當景氣敏感資產走弱，美債又恢復了以往上漲的避險作用。Bloomberg指出，過去一個月AI前景反覆變化，美債與那斯達克100指數呈負相關。

收盤殖利率曲線顯示，需求最強的是中天期債券。2年期殖利率下降1.09個基點至4.6829%，2年與10年期利差僅縮小0.31個基點至24.68個基點，大致持平；長債遭賣出，2年與30年期利差擴大2.44個基點至63.74個基點。過去一週，5年與10年期殖利率分別下降18.16與17.71個基點，2年與30年期則分別下降12.12與13.77個基點。

週二10年期殖利率的降幅幾乎全數來自通膨補償下降：損益兩平通膨率下降1.31個基點至2.1297%，實質殖利率僅微降0.09個基點至2.8%。過去一個月，名目殖利率下降6.48個基點，其中通膨補償下降22.33個基點，實質殖利率卻上升15.85個基點。因此，近期名目公債回升，對扣除通膨後融資成本的紓解並不一致。

油價盤中反彈，但仍明顯低於一個月前。WTI期貨上漲1.90%至每桶$81.69，布蘭特原油上漲1.90%至$91.07；兩者過去一個月仍分別下跌19.07%與18.47%。Bloomberg利率報導將這段期間的油價下跌，連結至通膨及緊縮預期降溫，並指出週二油價回升，是美債回吐部分盤中漲幅的原因之一。黃金期貨下跌2.64%至每盎司$3,555.10，美元指數下跌0.47%至103.826。

上午公布的經濟資料中，家庭信心大幅優於預期，就業與企業活動則有強有弱。世界大型企業研究會11月消費者信心指數由修正後的91.9躍升至103.3，遠高於TradingCharts所列的市場共識92.25；Bloomberg形容這是近兩年最強的信心水準。零售商業績也顯示支出持續：百思買受惠於電腦與新產品需求，調高全年展望；消費者尋找較便宜的日常必需品與節慶商品，則推動Dollar Tree銷售優於預期。

截至11月21日當週，Redbook零售銷售年增率由9.5%加快至11.3%。ADP另行公布的每週就業觀察顯示，四週平均新增僱用人數由23,000人降至21,000人。這項資料不同於ADP月度就業報告；在零售及信心轉強之際，它顯示僱用動能略為放緩。

區域企業指標也呈分歧。里奇蒙聯準銀行11月製造業綜合指數由-2升至3，高於預估的1，出貨指數由0升至2；服務業營收指數則由2降至-7。製造業改善的同時，區域服務業營收的表現轉弱。

9月房價指標顯示，月度動能有限。FHFA房價指數為444.4，前值444.3；公布的月增率為0.0%，低於修正後前值0.2%及預估的0.3%，年增率則由2.4%小幅升至2.5%。標普／凱斯席勒20大城市房價年增率由2.7%降至2.56%，經季節調整的月增率為0.1%，低於預估及前值的0.2%；未經季節調整的月度房價指標下跌0.5%，前月下跌0.4%。

中午，聯準會公布工業生產年度修訂，調整了歷年成長的分布與產能擴張速度估計。10月總產出仍較2022年底高3.6%，與先前估計相同。2023與2024年各年的成長率平均上修約0.5個百分點，2025年則下修0.5個百分點。2022年以來估計的年均產能成長率由1.2%降至1.0%，低於1972至2025年的平均1.9%。這次基準修訂未改變累計產出增幅，但在相同產出增幅下，估計的產能擴張較少。

聯準會政策展望持續限制債市漲勢。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams週一談話的進一步報導顯示，只要經濟條件有需要，他不排除連續幾次會議升息。週二公布的10月貼現率會議紀錄，則提供了另一項制度層面的訊號：在10月FOMC決定維持利率之前，已有八家地區聯準銀行董事會建議，將這項貸款利率由4%調高至4.25%。

這八家為波士頓、克里夫蘭、芝加哥、聖路易、明尼亞波利斯、里奇蒙、堪薩斯市及達拉斯。董事會建議針對的是由聯準會理事會決定的貼現率，可能與各行總裁在FOMC的立場不同。克里夫蘭總裁Beth Hammack在10月會議投下異議票，支持升息0.25個百分點；達拉斯總裁Lorie Logan與明尼亞波利斯總裁Neel Kashkari雖然各自董事會建議調高貼現率，仍投票支持維持政策利率。

債市回升期間，一筆大規模中天期美債標售獲市場吸收。$700億的5年期公債以4.719%得標殖利率完成標售，較下午1時投標截止前的市場殖利率高出不到0.5個基點。直接投標人獲配比例達創紀錄的36.7%，一級交易商僅承接9%，為2004年開始的紀錄中最低水準之一；投標倍數由2.33提高至2.37。Bloomberg指出，前一週公布標售時，市場預期的殖利率比此次得標水準高出逾20個基點。

部位調整也為整體債市回升增添動能。美國銀行模型估計，商品交易顧問（CTA）的美債空頭部位已減至9月高峰的約一半。資產規模$50億的iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF，截至週一的存續期間空頭曝險縮減至-6.4年，一週前為-7.1年。美國銀行的Chintan Kotecha估計，若曲線各天期殖利率再下降20至25個基點，多數剩餘CTA空頭部位將會平倉。

期貨市場仍預期政策進一步收緊，選擇權市場則顯示，投資人正付費防範更明顯的經濟放緩。Bloomberg週二報導指出，市場預期聯準會還會升息75個基點，至2027年中利率約為4.5%；投資人同時買入SOFR買權，避險利率其後轉向、至2028年初最低降至3%的情境。自11月初以來，對景氣放緩敏感的中期曲線買權未平倉量增加130萬口，增幅接近反向部位的六倍。過去一週，10年期美債期貨選擇權也轉為買權溢價較高，反映防範債券上漲的需求增加。

## AI信用受挫與新融資條件

CoreWeave多檔債券回吐週一漲幅，跌幅足以再創新低。據紐約時間下午1時36分報導的TRACE成交資料，2031年到期、票息9%的債券一度下跌3.6個價格點至面額的76.6%，2032年到期、票息9.625%的債券一度下跌4.6個價格點至74.9%。兩者分別於2025年7月及2026年6月發行，均跌至發行以來最低價。

賣壓也波及其他債券。2031年到期、票息9.75%的債券下跌3.75個價格點至面額的76.3%，為4月發售以來最低；2030年到期、票息9.25%的債券下跌3個價格點至80.9%，創2025年5月以來最低價。如此廣泛的重定價，使融資風險與股市對AI投資循環的疑慮一同重回焦點。

美國整體高收益債利差小幅擴大。計入配息後，HYG報酬率為-0.12%，LQD為-0.13%，EMB為-0.34%。相較CoreWeave債券的跌幅，這些變動很小，突顯最劇烈的賣壓仍集中在特定借款人。

新報導也指出，能為AI下一階段擴張提供資金的投資人，正受到限制。Bloomberg的Odd Lots電子報形容，在產業大量舉債後，包括壽險公司在內的部分大型買家，已接近內部對單一發行人的集中度上限。該報導認為，看似不同的資料中心租約、晶片融資與超大規模雲端業者債券，最終可能都連結到相同終端客戶。對AI產業曝險已高的機構而言，這種重疊意味著，單靠抵押品結構調整，能再增加的投資容量有限。

Pimco投資長Daniel Ivascyn表示，過去一年，AI資本支出、金融市場估值與實體經濟的連結變強；潛在金融意外，以及既有商業模式受到顛覆，都是成長風險。Pimco已將非投資等級債券持倉降至2008年以來最低，主要基金則仍小幅加碼5至10年期美債，整體殖利率曲線配置維持中性。他表示，目前著重高品質債券與房貸資產，是為了保留流動性，並因應殖利率突然下降的情境。

經濟學家對AI帶來的經濟曝險有不同估計。穆迪分析首席經濟學家Mark Zandi估計，AI相關投資與消費，今年可能貢獻美國GDP成長的多達三分之一。Wolfe Research的Stephanie Roth認為，只要AI支出未實際萎縮，經濟應能承受投資成長放慢；但股市下跌若使消費減少，衝擊就可能更嚴重。這些評估顯示，成長風險同時來自企業投資及家庭財富。

貿易政策持續改變產業的營運條件。美國商務部將總部位於新加坡的Megaspeed，以及阿里巴巴在新加坡的一家子公司列入貿易黑名單，限制兩者在未取得許可下取得美國先進技術。中國則將暫停對美國實施鎵、鍺、銻出口限制的期限，延至1月底；原定週五到期。在華府收緊AI晶片取得管道之際，北京的決定保留了這條原料供應管道。

軟體融資方面，Hg旗下Visma暫緩近期在倫敦IPO的計畫後，正洽談最高€65億借款，用於再融資及支付股東股利。知情人士指出，美國銀行、DNB Carnegie及高盛主導這套方案，包括最高€25億的銀行定期貸款，以及明年初向機構投資人募集的最高€40億融資。

其中約€35億將用於償還既有借款，其餘支付股利。知情人士表示，Visma槓桿倍數約2倍，為這項擬議資本重組提供了空間。機構融資部分將包括槓桿貸款，也可能使用高收益債或私募信貸。若納入高收益債，其償還限制可能使IPO延後兩年。Hg也在考慮約18個月後出售股權，融資規模與時程均仍在討論。

醫療產業則出現較明確的企業交易承諾。賽諾菲同意以$410億收購Insmed，每股支付現金$175，較收購洽談消息傳出前的收盤價溢價46%。這是三年來最大的製藥業收購案，將為新任執行長Belen Garijo帶來兩項已上市肺部疾病療法，以及罕見疾病研發產品線，協助賽諾菲面對Dupixent即將失去專利保護。2026年全球已宣布的製藥與生技交易金額成長逾50%，至約$2,950億。在資本市場已承接大規模科技投資之際，這筆交易又增加了一項大型現金收購。

財務陷入困境的借款人，則展現另一種資本用途。Braskem自行申報的重整方案擬募股本資金$22.5億，其中$13億由主要股東或第三方提供承銷保證。持有受影響債務過半數的債權人已同意主要條件，容許最高$36億債務轉換為股權。11月22日期限屆滿後，公司向法院申請延長20個營業日，以敲定安排。Braskem明確表示，這些條件不具約束力，仍須進一步協商、完成文件及取得公司核准。

美國商用不動產方面，最新估價顯示，以波特蘭兩家希爾頓飯店作擔保的債券，即使是優先順位部分，也可能全額損失。Hilton Portland Downtown與Duniway Portland合計估值約$5,800萬，較2019年的$3.403億下降83%；當年一筆$2.4億、僅付息的房貸被證券化。這兩處合計782間客房的物業，價值已不到債務的四分之一。

即使物業仍有這些價值，債券持有人也可能幾無回收，關鍵在於貸款服務機構的墊款。債券申報文件顯示，為支付成本所作的墊款約$5,300萬。若以估價金額出售，先償還墊款及其他費用後，包括原始評等AAA券別在內的債券持有人，可能幾乎或完全拿不到資金。損失須待出售時才會實現。完成法拍取得物業後，信託所述計畫是進行小幅改善，等待波特蘭旅宿業可能在2027至2028年復甦。

營運數據說明了這項計畫的難度。10月市中心商業區飯店平均住房率為62.9%，2019年10月則為79.5%，同期間每間可售客房收入下降31%。巴克萊估計，2027年將有逾$360億的單一資產、單一借款人CMBS到達最終到期日，超過今年規模的三倍。在更多類似結構即將面臨最終還款期限之際，波特蘭估價事件凸顯了服務費用優先受償的影響。消費信貸的另一則消息是，二手車銷售商兼次級貸款業者America's Car-Mart聲請破產。

## 能源成本轉嫁使央行維持緊縮立場

加拿大央行總裁Tiff Macklem警告，春季以來累積的能源成本，將愈來愈多地轉嫁給消費者，使通膨更具持續性，而經濟表現也比預期強韌。他表示，企業迄今已吸收大部分成本增加，但根據過去的遞延效應及央行調查，未來一年轉嫁程度將提高。

談話後，加拿大公債遭到拋售。渥太華時間下午5時，2年期殖利率約上升5個基點至3.268%，10年期約上升0.5個基點至3.691%；加幣一度升值0.67%，至每美元兌C$1.4266。隔夜交換市場反映的12月9日升息機率接近80%，高於當日稍早的約70%。

Macklem承認，原油價格與煉油利潤下降，意味通膨可能略低於先前預期。不過，央行管理委員會表示，當供給衝擊規模大、持續久或波及廣泛，需求仍強，或通膨預期上升時，政策可能需要提早或更有力地回應。這項有條件的反應，讓成本轉嫁程度與經濟韌性成為政策評估核心。

央行在更新的五年政策架構下，也調整了描述與衡量基礎價格壓力的方式。整體CPI仍是唯一的2%通膨目標，核心指標則用於判斷前景。官員將主要觀察CPI-trim與CPIX，停用CPI-common。CPI-trim採用變動的籃子，剔除每月價格變動異常大的項目；CPIX則固定排除八類波動較大的項目，其中包括蔬果，而非所有食品。這些指標將納入更廣泛的觀察架構，並一併檢視通膨擴散程度。

這項溝通調整，發生在多項核心指標接近2%、整體通膨卻超過3%之際。Macklem表示，央行在疫情復甦期間，過晚認清通膨的持續與擴散。他也承認，排除食品與汽油等顯著支出，讓家庭感到困惑；部分市場參與者則認為央行改變了通膨目標的判斷標準。

歐元區方面，來自立陶宛的歐洲央行管理委員會成員Gediminas Simkus主張，政策應進入略具限制性的水準。基礎通膨達2.6%、經濟具韌性且成長接近潛力，以及歐元近期貶值，都使他擔憂價格壓力正從能源擴散。他重申支持12月升息，並表示，若通膨持續，2027年可能還要進一步緊縮。

Simkus表示，薪資尚未出現明顯反應，但在整體通膨達4%、先前價格衝擊記憶猶新之際，德國與法國的薪資談判將很重要。愛沙尼亞的Ulo Kaasik另表示，最新資訊證實需要提高利率，讓通膨回到接近2%。他強調，能源成本擴散至其他價格的風險相當大，同時認為前景高度不確定。兩人的說法，為支持進一步緊縮的陣營增添了來自不同國家的聲音。

Simkus也支持可能將銀行最低準備率，由存款及其他負債的1%提高至2%。官員預定當週討論此事，但意見仍有分歧。他認為，這是結構性的貨幣政策工具，可與可預測、漸進縮減超額流動性的做法並行。減少利息支出與央行虧損，在他的論述中屬次要考量；準備率水準與適用條件仍待討論。

英格蘭銀行決策官員Megan Greene更著重成品燃油成本與未來薪資。她認為，除非數據或戰事出現重大變化，否則適合進一步緊縮，並認為達成持久外交和解的可能性不高。英國能源帳單預計1月再上升26%。自6月以來一直支持升息的Greene表示，經濟閒置程度已達高峰，前瞻指標顯示薪資成長可能維持約3.5%，高於符合通膨目標的速度。即使生產力改善，投入成本上升也可能讓企業更難吸收這樣的薪資增幅。

墨西哥央行11月意外降息後，新公布的通膨數據呈現不同訊號。11月上半月整體通膨由10月下半月的3.88%加快至3.96%，高於預估的3.92%；核心通膨則由3.82%降至3.68%，低於市場共識3.86%，降幅超出預期。決策者面對的是基礎價格壓力轉緩，但整體通膨仍接近央行容忍區間上緣的組合。

## 亞洲債市上漲，南韓政策分歧擴大

日本公債在三天假期後恢復交易時上漲，同時本地科技股補漲，反映週一美股回升。10年期殖利率下降7個基點至2.715%，5年期下降5.5個基點至2.125%，日經指數盤中一度上漲5%。隆奧的Homin Lee指出，市場對能源供應中斷及聯準會2027年政策路徑的預期轉趨平穩，支撐了上午的債市漲勢。

法國巴黎銀行資產管理的Ryutaro Kimura表示，空頭回補是長天期殖利率下降的推力之一，但大型本國機構似乎仍在觀望輝達消息的影響。他也指出，AI類股轉強，可能使日本央行12月升息的可能性再度浮現。

新財報顯示，殖利率提高已在改變壽險公司的投資組合。日本四大壽險公司在4至9月出售公債及其他本國債券，認列合計逾¥1.2兆、約合$75億的損失。它們處分過去低利率時買進的證券，將資金轉投殖利率較高的標的，以接受當期已實現損失，換取未來利息收入改善。

明治安田的損失增加49%至¥3,956億，住友生命增至¥937億，超過原來的三倍；日本生命為¥3,881億，較一年前減少約20%。第一生命已於11月13日公布¥3,339億損失，約為一年前的四倍。最新業績補齊了四家公司的整體情況，也量化這批重要本國投資人調整部位的成本。

澳洲債市朝連續第六天上漲邁進，將是6月以來最長連漲，投資人由原本預期繼續緊縮，轉向預期降息。週二交易中，10年期殖利率下降6個基點至4.84%，創7月10日以來最低，3年期下降4個基點。3年期殖利率過去一週已下降約30個基點，低於澳洲央行現金利率的幅度，擴大至2025年8月以來最大。

Bloomberg按會議日期對應的交換價格顯示，市場預期明年降息兩次，首次在5月降息的機率超過一半。在前一週就業數據公布前，市場原本反映2027年初升息的機率約三分之一。澳盛銀行週二預測首次降息將在6月。Yarra Capital Management的Darren Langer認為，轉變源於今年五次升息造成的損害開始浮現；但能否降息，仍取決於勞動市場持續惡化及CPI降溫。

南韓則面對不同的政策難題：晶片出口繁榮，家庭需求卻疲弱。第3季GDP季增1%，民間消費則萎縮0.2%；10月整體及核心通膨均為2.8%。當月就業人數減少50,000人，失業率卻降至2.5%，原因是有人退出勞動市場。青年就業人數創2020年以來同期10月最低。

高盛經濟學家Goohoon Kwon週二主張，由於進口成本的影響大於內需強度，穩定韓元會比進一步升息更能抑制通膨。他預期通膨於2027年下半年回到約2%，政策利率高點不超過3.5%；他預測明年民間消費成長接近2%，低於逾3%的整體經濟成長。

Kwon區分了記憶體晶片漲價與更廣泛的產量增加：獲利集中在兩家晶片商，可能需要時間才能傳到供應商與家庭。他預期，企業獲利帶來的稅款、股利及薪資支付，將形成龐大韓元需求，明年可能超過GDP的10%，達今年水準的三至四倍，並預測匯率為每美元兌1,280韓元。他表示，後續降息的時間與幅度，部分取決於AI熱潮能持續多久。

其他指標顯示，融資需求正在降溫。第3季家庭貸款僅增加₩4.7兆，為2025年初以來最小增幅，因股市疲弱壓抑無擔保借款，住宅交易也減少。花旗的Jin-Wook Kim警告，Kospi指數下半年下跌逾40%，可能侵蝕家庭財富與支出。不過，出口商將收入換回韓元，使韓元當季對美元仍升值約1%。

政府也在考慮1月發行約$30億美元債，銀行本週正提交提案；政府並尋求國會授權，2027年可在海外發行最高$80億債券。這筆擬議發債將補充外匯存底，10月底存底接近$4,430億，為2022年5月以來最高。發行規模與時間仍取決於市場條件。

麥格理最新研究進一步觀察出口循環。Larry Hu與Yuxiao Zhang表示，費城半導體指數往往領先中國出口約兩季。即使週一反彈，該指數下半年仍下跌約33%，因此他們預期中國出口急增的勢頭將在2027年初放緩。其分析意味，若貿易無法再支撐成長，中國將更需要內需刺激；寬鬆規模則取決於科技股修正只是暫時，還是更為嚴重。

## 主權債務計畫面對財政限制

委內瑞拉公布多年來首份具實質內容的財務架構，為債權人評估大規模重整提供新的依據。政府文件顯示，2025年底公共債務達$2,375億，相當於GDP的242%。債券及貸款為$1,165億，占總額略逾49%；主要集中於委內瑞拉國家石油公司（PDVSA）的非金融性承諾為$673億，占28%；雙邊債務為$233億。

總額中有相當大部分，是公共部門內部的債權。丹佛大學經濟學家Francisco Rodriguez指出，政府實體彼此間的債務約$576億，包括PDVSA對公共機構約$350億的債務，以及公共機構持有約$230億債券。比較總債務與外部債權人所持債權時，這項組成至關重要。

政府認為債務已不可持續，將在改革計畫的最初12個月內推動重整列為優先工作。架構構想包括財政規則、可信的預算約束基準，以及統一匯率制度。經濟副總統Calixto Ortega表示，過程將以可持續、全面、誠信、透明及迅速為原則。

資料公布後，主權與PDVSA債券上漲。委內瑞拉2027年到期債券上漲逾3個價格點，至面額的47.8%，為約一週最高。安聯投資投資組合經理Alexander Robey表示，重整可考慮將本金與利息債權的價值減記50%，實際結果仍取決於債權人協商及油價。

政府架構預測，石油日產量將在十年內達到290萬桶，主要來自奧里諾科帶，但也承認基礎建設與投資限制，使復甦緩慢。官方預估2026年初級財政赤字為GDP的3.2%；石油權利金收入將由2026年的$90億增至2031年的$132億，政府支出占GDP比重則在同期由29.7%降至25.3%。未來十年實質經濟年增6.3%的預測，是這次債務規劃中相當積極的經濟假設。美國制裁仍阻止債權人直接接觸，以及委內瑞拉進入美國金融市場。

巴西取得範圍較小、但具體的立法進展。繼參議院前一週通過後，眾議院週一深夜以353票對128票批准魯拉的支出約束方案，並否決六項修正案。法案規定，當財政目標面臨威脅時，經通膨調整的支出成長上限由2.5%降至2%，並擴大凍結支出的空間、縮減部分稅務優惠。預期2027年仍可節省R$500億至R$600億，參議院協商讓步已使估計節省金額減少約R$10億。

週二，隨著報導指出魯拉支持進一步財政調整，巴西里爾表現優於區域其他貨幣。BBVA的Alejandro Cuadrado將相對韌性歸因於這些消息，但強調新增措施仍待落實。其他拉丁美洲貨幣受到整體減碼風險及金屬走弱的衝擊：哥倫比亞披索下跌2.6%，創5月以來最大單日跌幅，本地對財政改革遭削弱的擔憂，加重了全球壓力。銅價走弱也拖累智利與秘魯貨幣。

塞內加爾方面，摩根士丹利對重整時程的評估較悲觀。策略師Neville Mandimika表示，預算爭議使雙邊與商業債權人的協調再添延誤因素，IMF執行董事會也尚未批准。他質疑政府年底前完成重整的目標，並認為，即使IMF接受預算政令，圍繞中期財政架構的政治分歧仍可能妨礙執行。

塞內加爾2031年到期債券報價接近面額的47%，11月前17個交易日中已有12天下跌。Bloomberg比較顯示，該國各天期公債當月合計下跌7.2%，是僅次於阿根廷、表現第二差的新興市場。Mandimika的重整情境顯示，債權價值增加幅度不足以補償歐元計價2037年到期債券持有人，因模型中的展期而承受的影響。這些是該行對可能條件與估值的判斷，協商及官方融資均尚未定案。

奈及利亞央行則已決定維持利率23%，符合受訪八位經濟學家中五位的預期。總裁Olayemi Cardoso表示，保持緊縮有助通膨朝個位數目標下降；10月通膨已由14.6%降至14.1%。自9月降息350個基點以來，奈拉貶值近5%。Cardoso將近期波動歸因於季節性美元需求、提前避險，以及1月16日大選前的支出，並預期明年波動將緩和。他表示，外匯存底接近$550億，足以支應十個月進口。

Global Evolution增持烏干達本幣債券的動作，則顯示邊境市場的投資需求並不平均。這家管理總資產$210億的基金公司，在上月烏干達先令下跌8%、當局採取應對措施期間加碼；當局當時向外匯市場注入$6,800萬，並在緊急會議升息225個基點。該公司三檔邊境市場基金9月底合計資產$75億，今年扣除費用後報酬率為10%至15%。策略師Stephen Bailey-Smith表示，外國投資人的參與，也將部分全球波動傳導至奈及利亞、埃及與烏干達的部位。

法國最新預算進展，是總理Sebastien Lecornu在11月23日信函中要求修改原始草案，納入農業與教育支援，以及為達成2027年赤字占GDP 5%目標所需的額外節支。他希望避免以行政命令強行實施原案。因此，最終預算內容，以及採取何種憲政程序使其生效，都攸關財政調整。

美債市場的中介業務則面臨另一項結構性決策。知情人士表示，新的結算要求推高成本，德國商業銀行正考慮縮減美國業務，選項包括退出附買回市場，以及在現券美債業務與券商合作。這項討論也適逢裕信銀行計畫收購該行，以及縮減其國際業務布局的策略。德國商業銀行拒絕評論可能的調整。

## 後市關注重點

下一個美國政策檢驗集中在11月25日週三美東時間上午8時30分。10月核心PCE通膨預估月增0.3%，與前值相同，年增率則預估為3.2%，前值3.1%。Bloomberg利率報導另列整體PCE預估為月增0.3%、年增3.8%。過去一個月油價下降，但市場仍擔憂基礎價格壓力持續，整體與核心通膨的差異將很重要。

同一時間還將公布10月耐久財訂單，預估成長0.4%，前值1.8%；第3季GDP第二次估值，市場共識為成長3.4%；以及截至11月21日當週初領失業救濟金人數，預估200,000人，前值203,000人。週二信心大幅上升、ADP僱用放緩，以及里奇蒙製造業與服務業分歧，顯示經濟訊號強弱不一，這批數據將進一步檢驗這些經濟訊號的整體平衡。債市定價仍有待釐清：持續通膨與實際成長，將如何與防範政策最終反轉的避險部位相互作用。

南韓週四決策雖有高度共識，分歧仍具重要影響。Bloomberg調查23位經濟學家，其中21位預期升息0.25個百分點至3.25%，高盛則預期不變。決議預定於首爾時間上午9時50分左右公布，聲明於上午10時30分前發布，總裁申鉉松記者會約在上午11時10分。更新的成長預測與六個月後利率預測中位數，將顯示官員如何權衡半導體繁榮與家庭需求疲弱。上次利率預測中位數為3.25%；若上調，將指向預期此次升息之外的進一步緊縮。

日本週三40年期公債標售，將在假期後恢復交易的漲勢，以及最新壽險投資組合損失披露之後，檢驗長天期需求。澳洲降息預期已明顯提前，勞動市場是否持續疲弱、消費者物價是否降溫，將決定首次降息時點。加拿大12月9日政策定價，現在更重視Macklem對能源成本延後轉嫁的警告；英格蘭銀行將於12月17日決策，Greene則持續強調成品燃油成本與薪資成長的持續性。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries recovered as renewed selling in artificial-intelligence stocks and reports of another U.S. tariff round revived demand for safety, but the gains stopped short of the longest maturities. The five-year yield fell 2.87 basis points to 4.7331% and the 10-year declined 1.4 basis points to 4.9297%, while the 30-year rose 1.35 basis points to 5.3203%. Stronger consumer confidence and a rebound in oil restrained the advance as investors continued to anticipate Federal Reserve tightening.

The retreat from technology risk was sharper in individual corporate bonds. CoreWeave securities erased Monday's recovery and traded at record lows, while broad U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly. Nvidia's leadership reversal had restored confidence for a session; Tuesday's trading returned attention to the cost and availability of capital across the AI industry.

Monetary-policy signals remained restrictive in several economies. Canada's central bank warned that accumulated energy costs would increasingly reach consumers, and European and British officials pressed the case for further increases. Australia's bond rally, driven by growing expectations of rate cuts, illustrated the different growth conditions emerging beneath the global inflation debate. New sovereign debt disclosures in Venezuela and a proposed multibillion-euro Visma financing added substantial borrower-specific news beyond the daily Treasury move.

## Treasury Recovery Meets Firmer U.S. Data

The U.S. session reversed part of Monday's withdrawal from havens as investors again questioned the durability of technology investment. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.99% to 26,214.17 and the semiconductor index dropped 7.88%. Nvidia lost about 6%, and Anthropic fell below its $83 IPO price. The S&P 500's smaller 0.50% decline to 7,201.09 concealed a less uniform market: most constituents advanced, and the Dow gained 0.9%.

Selling accelerated after reports that Washington was preparing tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies. People familiar with the plans said the measures would replace levies struck down by the Supreme Court. Chinese products were expected to face broader coverage than goods from other countries, but the additional duties would keep overall rates within the levels agreed in individual trade deals. The measures were being prepared economy by economy, rather than as a blanket tariff.

That distinction matters to the prospective scale of the trade shock. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative was expected to conclude its Section 301 investigation into excess manufacturing capacity, providing the basis for the planned action. Tuesday's Treasury buying accompanied the equity response to those reports, with renewed trade uncertainty adding to concerns about AI demand.

Bloomberg's intraday rates account put the 10-year yield around 4.90%, a two-week low, before stronger consumer confidence and recovering crude prices pared the gains. The closing yield of 4.9297% consequently represented a much smaller advance in bond prices. Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Lindsay Rosner said Treasuries had resumed their familiar role of appreciating when economically sensitive assets weakened. Bloomberg reported a negative relationship between Treasuries and the Nasdaq 100 over the past month as the AI outlook swung.

The closing curve showed the strongest demand in intermediate debt. The two-year yield declined 1.09 basis points to 4.6829%, leaving the two- to 10-year spread almost unchanged at 24.68 basis points, down 0.31 basis point. The two- to 30-year gap widened 2.44 basis points to 63.74 as the long bond sold off. Over the week, five- and 10-year yields were down 18.16 and 17.71 basis points, respectively, compared with a 12.12-basis-point fall at two years and 13.77 at 30 years.

Lower inflation compensation accounted for nearly all of Tuesday's 10-year decline. The breakeven fell 1.31 basis points to 2.1297%, while the real yield edged down 0.09 basis point to 2.8%. Over the month, the nominal yield was 6.48 basis points lower, combining a 22.33-basis-point decline in inflation compensation with a 15.85-basis-point increase in real yields. The recent recovery in nominal government debt has therefore offered uneven relief to inflation-adjusted financing costs.

Oil rebounded during the session while remaining substantially below its month-earlier level. WTI futures rose 1.90% to $81.69 a barrel and Brent gained 1.90% to $91.07; their monthly declines were 19.07% and 18.47%. Bloomberg's rates reporting linked the broader oil decline to reduced inflation and tightening expectations, while identifying Tuesday's recovery as one reason Treasuries surrendered some intraday gains. Gold futures fell 2.64% to $3,555.10 an ounce, and the dollar index declined 0.47% to 103.826.

The morning's economic releases provided a substantial household-confidence surprise alongside mixed labor and business observations. Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 in November from a revised 91.9, against the 92.25 consensus reported by TradingCharts. Bloomberg described confidence as the strongest in nearly two years. Retailer results also pointed to continuing spending: Best Buy raised its annual outlook on demand for computing and newer products, while Dollar Tree's sales exceeded expectations as shoppers sought cheaper essentials and holiday purchases.

Redbook's annual sales growth accelerated to 11.3% for the week of November 21 from 9.5%. ADP's separate weekly employment observation showed a four-week-average hiring pace of 21,000, down from 23,000. The latter supplies a modest slowing in hiring momentum alongside stronger retail and confidence readings; it is distinct from ADP's monthly employment report.

Regional business indicators diverged. The Richmond Fed manufacturing composite rose to 3 in November from minus 2, exceeding the forecast of 1, and shipments improved to 2 from zero. The Richmond services revenues index moved the other way, falling to minus 7 from 2. The manufacturing improvement thus arrived with a weaker observation on regional services revenue.

September house-price measures showed limited monthly momentum. The FHFA index stood at 444.4 against 444.3 previously, with its published monthly change at 0.0% after a revised 0.2% increase and a 0.3% forecast. Annual FHFA inflation edged up to 2.5% from 2.4%. S&P/Case-Shiller's 20-city annual increase slowed to 2.56% from 2.7%; the seasonally adjusted 20-city monthly gain was 0.1%, below both the 0.2% forecast and prior reading. Its unadjusted monthly home-price measure fell 0.5% after a 0.4% decline.

At noon, the Fed's annual industrial-production revision changed the historical composition of growth and the estimated pace of capacity expansion. Total production in October remained 3.6% above the end of 2022, unchanged from the earlier estimate. Annual growth in 2023 and 2024 was raised by about 0.5 percentage point per year on average, while the 2025 pace was reduced by 0.5 point. Estimated annual capacity growth since 2022 fell to 1.0% from 1.2%, below the 1.9% average over 1972-2025. The benchmark leaves the cumulative production gain intact while depicting less expansion in the capacity available to accommodate it.

The Fed's policy outlook continued to constrain the rally. Further reporting of New York Fed President John Williams' Monday remarks showed that he would not rule out increases at successive meetings if economic conditions warranted them. Tuesday's release of October discount-rate minutes supplied a different institutional signal: eight regional bank boards had recommended lifting that lending rate to 4.25% from 4% before the October FOMC hold.

Those boards were Boston, Cleveland, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Richmond, Kansas City and Dallas. Their recommendations concern the discount rate set by the Board of Governors and can differ from their presidents' FOMC positions. Cleveland President Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase at the October meeting, while Dallas President Lorie Logan and Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari voted for the hold despite their boards' recommendations.

Demand absorbed a large intermediate-maturity Treasury sale during the recovery. The $70 billion five-year auction cleared at 4.719%, less than half a basis point above the yield just before the 1 p.m. bidding deadline. Direct bidders received a record 36.7%, while primary dealers took only 9%, among the lowest shares in records extending to 2004. Bid-to-cover improved to 2.37 from 2.33. Bloomberg noted that the expected yield when the sale was announced the previous week had been more than 20 basis points higher.

Positioning added momentum to the broader bond recovery. A Bank of America model estimated that commodity trading advisers had reduced Treasury shorts to about half their September peak. The $5 billion iMGP DBi Managed Futures Strategy ETF cut its short duration exposure to negative 6.4 years as of Monday from negative 7.1 a week earlier. Bank of America's Chintan Kotecha estimated that a further 20-25-basis-point decline in yields across the curve would unwind most remaining CTA shorts.

Options showed investors paying for a more pronounced economic slowdown even while futures anticipated additional restraint. Bloomberg's Tuesday account put the expected Fed rate near 4.5% by mid-2027 after another 75 basis points of increases. Calls on SOFR were being used to hedge a subsequent shift toward rates as low as 3% by early 2028. Open interest in slowdown-sensitive mid-curve calls had increased by 1.3 million contracts since the start of November, nearly six times the increase on the opposing side. Ten-year Treasury futures options had also shifted toward a premium for calls over the preceding week, reflecting greater demand to protect against a bond rally.

## AI Credit Losses and New Financing Terms

CoreWeave's bonds reversed Monday's gains with losses large enough to establish new lows across several issues. Its 9% notes due in 2031 fell as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents on the dollar, according to TRACE trading reported at 1:36 p.m. New York time. The 9.625% 2032 notes dropped as much as 4.6 points to 74.9 cents. Both traded at their lowest prices since issuance, in July 2025 and June 2026 respectively.

The pressure extended to its other debt. The 9.75% 2031 issue fell 3.75 points to 76.3 cents, a low since its April sale, and the 9.25% 2030 bonds lost 3 points to 80.9 cents, their weakest since May 2025. The breadth of the repricing put financing risk back alongside the equity market's doubts about the AI investment cycle.

Broad U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly. Including distributions, HYG returned minus 0.12%, LQD lost 0.13% and EMB declined 0.34%. Those changes were small beside CoreWeave's bond losses, underscoring the concentration of the most severe selling in particular borrowers.

New reporting also identified constraints on who can finance the next stage of AI expansion. Bloomberg's Odd Lots newsletter described some large buyers, including life insurers, approaching internal issuer-concentration limits after the industry's heavy borrowing. In its assessment, apparently different exposures through data-center leases, chip financing and hyperscaler bonds can converge on the same end customers. That overlap reduces the scope for collateral structures alone to create additional investment capacity at institutions already heavily exposed to the sector.

Pimco chief investment officer Daniel Ivascyn said the connection between AI capital spending, financial-market valuations and the real economy had strengthened over the past year. He cited possible financial accidents and disruption of established business models as risks to growth. Pimco had reduced below-investment-grade holdings to their lowest level since 2008, while its principal funds remained slightly overweight five- to 10-year Treasuries and broadly neutral on the curve. His comments framed the firm's current emphasis on high-quality bonds and mortgages around liquidity and resilience to a sudden decline in yields.

Economists supplied different estimates of the economic exposure. Moody's Analytics chief economist Mark Zandi estimated that AI-related investment and consumption could account for as much as a third of U.S. GDP growth this year. Wolfe Research's Stephanie Roth judged that the economy could absorb slower AI investment provided spending did not contract outright, while identifying a stock-market-driven reduction in consumption as a way the effects could become more severe. Those assessments locate the growth risk in both business investment and household wealth.

Trade policy continued to change the industry's operating conditions. The Commerce Department added Singapore-based Megaspeed and a Singaporean Alibaba subsidiary to its trade blacklist, restricting access to advanced U.S. technology without a license. China, meanwhile, extended its suspension of restrictions on exports of gallium, germanium and antimony to the United States until the end of January. The suspension had been due to expire on Friday. Beijing's decision preserved that supply channel as Washington tightened controls on access to AI chips.

Elsewhere in software finance, Hg-owned Visma was working on up to EUR6.5 billion of borrowing to refinance debt and pay a shareholder dividend after shelving a near-term London IPO. People familiar with the discussions said Bank of America, DNB Carnegie and Goldman Sachs were leading a package comprising as much as EUR2.5 billion of bank term debt and up to EUR4 billion to be marketed to institutional investors early next year.

About EUR3.5 billion would refinance existing borrowings, with the remainder earmarked for the dividend. Visma's leverage of about 2 times gave it room for the proposed recapitalization, according to the people. The institutional portion would include leveraged loans and could also involve high-yield bonds or private credit. A high-yield component could delay an IPO for two years because of repayment restrictions attached to that debt. Hg was also considering selling an equity stake in about 18 months; the financing's size and timing remained under discussion.

Healthcare produced a firmer corporate commitment. Sanofi agreed to acquire Insmed for $41 billion, paying $175 a share in cash, a 46% premium to the target's closing price before reports of the talks. The largest pharmaceutical acquisition in three years would give new chief executive Belen Garijo two marketed lung-disease treatments and a rare-disease pipeline as Sanofi approaches the loss of patent protection on Dupixent. Announced pharmaceutical and biotechnology transactions worldwide had risen more than 50% to about $295 billion in 2026. The acquisition adds a major cash transaction to a capital market already accommodating substantial technology investment.

Distressed borrowers showed a different use of capital. Braskem's own filing put the proposed equity raising in its restructuring at $2.25 billion, including a $1.3 billion backstop from principal shareholders or third parties. Creditors holding a majority of the affected debt had agreed on main terms that would permit conversion of up to $3.6 billion into equity. The company sought a 20-business-day court extension to finalize the arrangement after its November 22 deadline. Braskem expressly described the terms as nonbinding and subject to further negotiation, documentation and corporate approvals.

In U.S. commercial property, new appraisals pointed to a potentially complete loss even for the senior bonds backed by two Portland Hilton hotels. The Hilton Portland Downtown and Duniway Portland were valued at about $58 million combined, down 83% from $340.3 million in 2019, when a $240 million interest-only mortgage was securitized. The 782-room properties were worth less than one-quarter of the debt.

Servicer advances explain why even that residual property value may offer little recovery. About $53 million had been advanced to meet costs, according to bond filings. Repaying those advances and other expenses after a sale at the appraised value would leave little or nothing for bondholders, including the tranche originally rated AAA. Losses will crystallize only when a sale occurs. Following foreclosure, the trust's stated plan was to make minor improvements and await a possible recovery in Portland hospitality in 2027-2028.

The operating figures showed the challenge to that plan. Central-business-district hotel occupancy averaged 62.9% in October against 79.5% in October 2019, and revenue per available room was down 31% over that period. Barclays estimated that more than $36 billion of single-asset, single-borrower CMBS would reach final maturity in 2027, over three times this year's volume. The Portland valuation exposes the repayment priority of servicing costs at a point when more comparable structures are approaching final deadlines. In another part of consumer credit, used-car seller and subprime lender America's Car-Mart filed for bankruptcy.

## Energy Pass-Through Sustains Central-Bank Restraint

Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem warned that energy costs accumulated since the spring would increasingly be passed on to consumers, adding persistence to inflation while the economy proved more resilient than expected. Businesses had absorbed much of the increase so far, he said, but historical lags and the bank's surveys pointed to more pass-through over the coming year.

Canadian bonds sold off following the remarks. At 5 p.m. Ottawa time, two-year yields were about 5 basis points higher at 3.268%, while 10-year yields were up about 0.5 basis point at 3.691%. The Canadian dollar strengthened as much as 0.67% to C$1.4266 per U.S. dollar. Overnight swaps put the probability of a December 9 increase near 80%, up from about 70% earlier in the day.

Macklem acknowledged that lower crude prices and refinery margins suggested inflation might be somewhat lower than previously expected. The bank's governing council nevertheless said policy could need to respond earlier or more forcefully when supply shocks were large, persistent or broad-based, when demand remained strong, or when inflation expectations rose. That conditional response places the degree of pass-through and the economy's resilience at the center of its assessment.

The bank also changed how it will describe and measure underlying pressure under its renewed five-year framework. Headline CPI remains the exclusive 2% target, while core indicators inform the outlook. Officials will focus primarily on CPI-trim and CPIX and discontinue CPI-common. CPI-trim removes unusually large monthly price changes using a variable basket; CPIX consistently excludes eight volatile categories, including fruit and vegetables rather than all food. The measures will sit within a broader dashboard that includes inflation breadth.

That communication change arrives while several core measures are running near 2% and headline inflation exceeds 3%. Macklem said the bank had been too slow during the pandemic recovery to recognize the persistence and spread of inflation. He also acknowledged confusion among households about excluding prominent expenses such as food and gasoline, and a perception among some market participants that the bank had shifted its inflation goalposts.

In the euro area, Lithuanian Governing Council member Gediminas Simkus advocated moving policy into mildly restrictive territory. Underlying inflation of 2.6%, a resilient economy growing near potential and the euro's recent depreciation supported his concern that pressure was broadening beyond energy. He reiterated support for a December increase and said persistent inflation could require more tightening in 2027.

Simkus said wages had not yet shown a material response, but negotiations in Germany and France would be important with headline inflation at 4% and memories of the earlier price shock still fresh. Estonia's Ulo Kaasik separately said the latest information confirmed a need for higher rates to restore inflation near 2%. He emphasized a substantial risk of energy costs spreading into other prices while describing the outlook as highly uncertain. Their comments added distinct national voices to the coalition seeking further restraint.

Simkus also backed a possible increase in banks' minimum reserve requirement to 2% of deposits and other liabilities from 1%. Officials were due to discuss the issue during the week and remained divided. He regarded the measure as a structural monetary-policy tool compatible with a predictable, gradual reduction in excess liquidity. Reduced interest payments and central-bank losses were secondary considerations in his argument; the level and conditions still required discussion.

Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene put greater emphasis on refined-fuel costs and prospective wages. She said further tightening was appropriate unless data or the war changed dramatically, and viewed a lasting diplomatic settlement as unlikely. UK energy bills were expected to rise another 26% in January. Greene, who had favored increases since June, said slack had peaked and forward-looking indicators suggested wage growth could remain around 3.5%, above a pace consistent with the inflation target. Rising input costs could make such wage gains harder to absorb even if productivity improved.

Mexico's new inflation release contained competing signals after Banxico's surprise November cut. Headline inflation accelerated to 3.96% in the first half of November from 3.88% in the second half of October, exceeding the 3.92% forecast. Core inflation eased more than expected, falling to 3.68% from 3.82% against a 3.86% consensus. That split gives policymakers a softer underlying reading alongside a headline rate still near the upper edge of the central bank's tolerance band.

## Asian Bonds Gain as Korea's Policy Divide Widens

Japanese government bonds rallied on their return from a three-day holiday even as local technology shares caught up with Monday's U.S. recovery. The 10-year yield fell 7 basis points to 2.715% and the five-year declined 5.5 basis points to 2.125%, while the Nikkei rose as much as 5% intraday. Lombard Odier's Homin Lee pointed to calmer expectations for energy disruption and the Fed's 2027 path as support for the morning's bond gains.

BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura identified short-covering as a force behind lower long-end yields, while saying major domestic institutions appeared to be waiting to assess the implications of the Nvidia news. He also noted that stronger AI shares could revive the possibility of a December Bank of Japan increase. The rally therefore developed while the policy outlook and the participation of large domestic buyers remained unsettled.

New earnings disclosures showed how higher yields were already changing insurers' portfolios. Japan's four largest life insurers booked more than JPY1.2 trillion, or $7.5 billion, of losses from sales of government and other domestic bonds in April-September. They were disposing of securities purchased at lower rates to reinvest at higher yields, accepting current realized losses to improve future interest income.

Meiji Yasuda's losses rose 49% to JPY395.6 billion and Sumitomo Life's increased more than threefold to JPY93.7 billion. Nippon Life reported JPY388.1 billion, about 20% less than a year earlier. Daiichi Life had reported JPY333.9 billion on November 13, roughly four times the year-earlier amount. The latest results completed the picture across the four firms and quantified the cost of repositioning a major domestic investor base.

Australia's market was approaching a sixth consecutive daily gain, its longest run since June, as investors shifted from expecting more tightening toward cuts. Ten-year yields fell 6 basis points during Tuesday trading to 4.84%, their lowest since July 10, and three-year yields declined 4 basis points. Three-year yields had fallen about 30 basis points over the week and were at their largest discount to the RBA cash rate since August 2025.

Bloomberg's meeting-linked swaps showed two cuts expected next year and a better-than-even chance of the first in May. Before the previous week's employment figures, pricing had included roughly a one-in-three chance of an early-2027 increase. ANZ on Tuesday forecast a first cut in June. Yarra Capital Management's Darren Langer linked the change to emerging damage from this year's five increases, while making the prospect of easing conditional on continued labor-market deterioration and moderating CPI.

South Korea presented a different policy problem: booming chip exports alongside weak household demand. GDP grew 1% in Q3 from the previous quarter, while private consumption contracted 0.2%. October headline and core inflation were both 2.8%. Employment fell by 50,000 in the month even as the unemployment rate declined to 2.5%, with departures from the labor force explaining the lower rate. Youth employment reached its weakest October level since 2020.

Goldman Sachs economist Goohoon Kwon argued Tuesday that stabilizing the won would curb inflation more effectively than further rate increases because import costs were more important than domestic-demand strength. He expected inflation to return to about 2% in the second half of 2027 and the policy rate to peak no higher than 3.5%. His forecast for private consumption growth near 2% next year trailed overall growth above 3%.

Kwon distinguished higher memory-chip prices from broader increases in production volumes: profits concentrated at two chipmakers could take time to reach suppliers and households. He expected tax, dividend and wage payments from corporate profits to generate substantial demand for won, potentially more than 10% of GDP next year, three to four times this year's level, and forecast the currency at 1,280 per dollar. The timing and extent of later rate cuts, he said, would depend partly on the duration of the AI boom.

Other indicators showed financial demand cooling. Household loans rose only KRW4.7 trillion in Q3, their smallest increase since early 2025, as weaker equities constrained unsecured borrowing and housing transactions declined. Citigroup's Jin-Wook Kim warned that the Kospi's decline of more than 40% during the second half could erode household wealth and spending. The currency had nevertheless gained about 1% against the dollar during the quarter as exporters converted proceeds.

The government was also considering a roughly $3 billion dollar bond sale in January, with banks presenting proposals this week. It was seeking parliamentary authority for as much as $8 billion of offshore issuance in 2027. The prospective sale would support foreign-exchange reserves, which stood near $443 billion at the end of October, the highest since May 2022. The amount and timing remained dependent on market conditions.

Fresh Macquarie research looked further down the export cycle. Larry Hu and Yuxiao Zhang said the Philadelphia semiconductor index tended to lead Chinese exports by about two quarters. With the index still down about 33% in the second half even after Monday's rebound, they expected China's export surge to slow in early 2027. Their analysis implied a greater need for domestic stimulus if trade could no longer carry growth, with the scale of easing dependent on whether the technology correction proved temporary or more severe.

## Sovereign Debt Plans Confront Fiscal Constraints

Venezuela released its first substantial financial framework in years, giving creditors a new basis for assessing a sweeping restructuring. Public debt stood at $237.5 billion at the end of 2025, equivalent to 242% of GDP, according to the government's document. Bonds and loans accounted for $116.5 billion, just over 49% of the total, while nonfinancial commitments concentrated in PDVSA were $67.3 billion, or 28%. Bilateral debt was $23.3 billion.

The headline total includes substantial claims within the public sector. University of Denver economist Francisco Rodriguez identified about $57.6 billion owed by one government entity to another, including approximately $35 billion of PDVSA obligations to public institutions and about $23 billion of bonds held by public bodies. That composition is central to comparing the total with the claims of outside creditors.

The government described the debt as unsustainable and made restructuring within the first 12 months a priority of its reform plan. The framework envisaged fiscal rules, a credible budget anchor and a unified exchange-rate regime. Economy Vice President Calixto Ortega said the process would pursue sustainability, comprehensiveness, good faith, transparency and speed.

Sovereign and PDVSA bonds rallied on the disclosure. Venezuela's 2027 notes gained more than 3 cents to 47.8 cents on the dollar, their highest in about a week. Allianz Global Investors portfolio manager Alexander Robey said a possible 50% haircut to principal and interest claims could be considered, with outcomes dependent on creditor negotiations and oil prices. That scenario concerns the value of principal and interest claims, distinct from a quoted bond price or a final exchange offer.

The framework projected oil output reaching 2.9 million barrels a day over ten years, mainly from the Orinoco Belt, while acknowledging a slow recovery constrained by infrastructure and investment restrictions. Authorities forecast a 3.2% primary deficit in 2026, oil royalties increasing from $9 billion in 2026 to $13.2 billion in 2031, and government spending declining from 29.7% to 25.3% of GDP over the same period. Their projection of 6.3% annual real growth over the next decade supplies an ambitious economic assumption for the debt exercise. U.S. sanctions still prevent direct creditor engagement and access to U.S. financial markets.

Brazil achieved a narrower, concrete legislative advance. The lower house approved Lula's spending-restraint package by 353 votes to 128 late Monday after Senate passage the previous week. Deputies rejected six amendments. The legislation lowers the ceiling on inflation-adjusted spending growth to 2% from 2.5% when fiscal targets are threatened, expands scope to freeze expenditure and reduces selected tax benefits. Expected 2027 savings remain BRL50 billion-BRL60 billion, with Senate concessions having reduced the estimate by about BRL1 billion.

The real subsequently outperformed regional peers Tuesday as reports suggested Lula supported further fiscal adjustment. BBVA's Alejandro Cuadrado attributed the relative resilience to those reports while emphasizing that the additional measures still needed to materialize. Elsewhere, broad risk reduction and weaker metals hit Latin American currencies: Colombia's peso fell 2.6%, its worst session since May, with local concerns about the dilution of fiscal reform adding to global pressure. Chilean and Peruvian currencies also suffered as copper weakened.

In Senegal, Morgan Stanley supplied a more pessimistic assessment of restructuring timing. Strategist Neville Mandimika said the budget dispute added another source of delay to coordination among bilateral and commercial creditors, with IMF board approval still pending. He doubted the government's year-end completion objective and argued that political disagreement over the medium-term fiscal framework could impair implementation even if the IMF accepted budget decrees.

Senegal's 2031 notes were quoted near 47 cents after declining in 12 of November's first 17 trading sessions. Government bonds across maturities had lost 7.2% during the month, the second-weakest emerging-market performance after Argentina in Bloomberg's comparison. Mandimika's restructuring scenarios showed insufficient uplift in claims to compensate holders of the euro-denominated 2037 bonds for modeled maturity extensions. Those are the bank's prospective terms and valuation judgments as negotiations and official financing remain unresolved.

Nigeria's central bank delivered an actual policy hold at 23%, matching five of eight surveyed economists. Governor Olayemi Cardoso said maintaining restraint would support disinflation toward a single-digit goal after October inflation slowed to 14.1% from 14.6%. The naira had weakened almost 5% since September's 350-basis-point cut. Cardoso attributed recent volatility to seasonal dollar demand, advance hedging and spending ahead of the January 16 election, and expected it to moderate next year. He put reserves near $55 billion, sufficient for ten months of imports.

A separate fund-manager account highlighted the uneven appetite for frontier local debt. Global Evolution, which manages $21 billion overall, added Ugandan bonds during the response to last month's 8% shilling decline, when authorities injected $68 million into foreign exchange and raised rates 225 basis points at an emergency meeting. Its three frontier funds, with combined assets of $7.5 billion at September-end, had returned 10%-15% this year after fees. Strategist Stephen Bailey-Smith said foreign-investor participation had nevertheless transmitted some global volatility into positions in Nigeria, Egypt and Uganda.

France's latest budget contribution was a November 23 letter from Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu seeking revisions to the original draft to reflect farming and education support alongside additional savings needed for a 5% deficit target in 2027. He wanted to avoid imposing the original text by executive ordinance. That request makes the content of any eventual budget, as well as the constitutional route used to enact it, relevant to the fiscal adjustment.

Treasury-market intermediation faced a separate structural decision. Commerzbank was considering reducing its U.S. involvement as new clearing requirements raised costs, people familiar with the discussions said. Options included exiting repo and partnering with a broker-dealer in cash Treasuries. The deliberations also coincided with UniCredit's planned takeover and a strategy to reduce the bank's international presence. Commerzbank declined to comment on the potential changes.

## Forward Market Significance

Wednesday, November 25 concentrates the next U.S. policy test at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. October core PCE inflation is expected at 0.3% month on month, unchanged from the prior pace, and 3.2% annually against 3.1% previously. Bloomberg's rates account separately put expected headline PCE inflation at 0.3% monthly and 3.8% annually. The distinction between headline and core will matter as lower oil over the month coexists with concerns about persistent underlying pressure.

The same release window brings October durable-goods orders, forecast to rise 0.4% after 1.8%, Q3 GDP's second estimate, with a 3.4% consensus, and initial claims for the week of November 21, expected at 200,000 after 203,000. Those observations will test the balance exposed Tuesday by a large confidence increase, slower ADP hiring and contrasting Richmond manufacturing and services readings. In bond pricing, the open question is how persistent inflation and realized growth interact with hedges against an eventual policy reversal.

South Korea's Thursday decision has a strong consensus but a consequential disagreement. Twenty-one of 23 Bloomberg-surveyed economists expect a quarter-point increase to 3.25%; Goldman Sachs expects a hold. The decision is due around 9:50 a.m. Seoul time, the statement by 10:30 a.m. and Governor Shin Hyun Song's briefing around 11:10 a.m. Updated growth forecasts and the median six-month rate projection will indicate how officials weigh the semiconductor boom against household weakness. The previous projection median was 3.25%; a higher figure would point to additional tightening beyond the expected move.

Japan's Wednesday 40-year auction will test long-duration demand after the holiday reopening rally and the latest disclosure of insurer portfolio losses. Australia's newly advanced easing expectations leave the persistence of labor weakness and moderation in consumer prices central to the timing of a first cut. In Canada, December 9 policy pricing now gives greater weight to Macklem's warning about delayed energy pass-through; the Bank of England decides on December 17 with Greene emphasizing refined-fuel costs and wage persistence.

For credit, Visma's eventual financing mix will determine the division between bank, institutional and potentially private-credit funding, as well as constraints on a later listing. Braskem's requested extension leaves final documentation and approvals ahead of the proposed equity raising and conversion. Venezuela's new fiscal and debt figures create a basis for negotiations whose progress still depends on sanctions and creditor access, while Senegal's year-end objective remains exposed to agreement on the fiscal framework and IMF approval.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Renewed selling in AI shares and reports of planned U.S. tariffs on China, the European Union and other economies brought buyers back to Treasuries. Intermediate maturities led: the five-year yield fell 2.87 basis points to 4.7331% and the 10-year declined 1.4 basis points to 4.9297%, while the 30-year rose 1.35 basis points to 5.3203%. Lower inflation compensation accounted for nearly all the 10-year move: the breakeven fell 1.31 basis points and the real yield slipped 0.09 basis point.

Consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 from a revised 91.9, and an oil rebound helped pare earlier bond gains. Fed tightening expectations persisted alongside demand for options protecting against an eventual slowdown. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.99%, with semiconductor shares down 7.88%; CoreWeave bonds erased Monday's recovery and traded at record lows as broad U.S. high-yield spreads widened modestly. Investor concentration limits added constraints to AI financing. Separately, Visma was discussing up to EUR6.5 billion of borrowing for refinancing and a shareholder dividend after shelving a near-term IPO.

Canada's Tiff Macklem warned of delayed energy-cost pass-through, while European and British officials argued for further restraint. Australia's bond rally reflected growing expectations of cuts as labor conditions weakened. Venezuela's new debt and fiscal framework gave creditors a basis for restructuring discussions, with sanctions still preventing direct engagement. Wednesday's U.S. inflation and activity releases are the nearest test of how persistent price pressure and realized growth fit together.
